senses.sense_definition: Excessively complicated or intricate, especially regarding bureaucratic systems.

examples.text: The company struggled to navigate the <w>Byzantine</w> rules of the new tax law.
He was frustrated by the <w>Byzantine</w> procedures required to get a simple permit.

senses.sense_definition: Characterized by devious, secretive, or underhanded methods.

examples.text: The politician used <w>Byzantine</w> tactics to undermine his rivals behind the scenes.
Her <w>Byzantine</w> schemes were eventually uncovered by the investigative journalists.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the ancient city of Byzantium or the Eastern Roman Empire.

examples.text: The museum displayed several artifacts from the <w>Byzantine</w> era.
Historians often study the <w>Byzantine</w> influence on later European art.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to a style of architecture featuring domes on pendentives and elaborate mosaics.

examples.text: The cathedral is famous for its stunning <w>Byzantine</w> architecture and golden mosaics.
Many churches in the region were built in the traditional <w>Byzantine</w> style.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to the liturgical rites used by certain Eastern Orthodox and Greek Catholic churches.

examples.text: The choir performed chants according to the ancient <w>Byzantine</w> rite.
He attended a service conducted in the <w>Byzantine</w> tradition.

senses.sense_definition: A person who lived in Byzantium or the Byzantine Empire.

examples.text: The <w>Byzantines</w> were known for their sophisticated trade networks.
Many <w>Byzantines</w> fled to Italy after the fall of Constantinople.

senses.sense_definition: A deep, dark shade of violet color.

examples.text: The artist mixed a touch of <w>Byzantine</w> into the shadows of the painting.
The velvet curtains were dyed a rich <w>Byzantine</w>.
